messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and at a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a quick wash (soft cloth, mild cleaner) and tune it to standard tuning (E‑A‑D‑G‑B‑E). | A clean, well‑tuned instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take Quality Photos** | • Use natural light, avoid harsh shadows.
• Capture front, back, side, headstock, strings, and any visible wear.
• Include a reference object (e.g., a coin or a hand) for scale. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce questions about condition. | | **3. Write a Clear Description** | • Brand, model, year, wood type, finish, serial number.
• Mention any upgrades (new strings, pickups, hardware).
• Note any imperfections (scratches, cracks, fret wear).
• State whether it’s still in its original case. | Transparency builds trust and speeds up negotiations. | | **4. Research Pricing** | • Check recent sales on eBay, Reverb, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local music stores.
• Compare similar models, age, and condition. | Helps set a realistic asking price and gives you leverage during bargaining. | | **5. Choose Your Selling Platform(s)** | • **Online Marketplaces** – eBay, Reverb, Etsy (for vintage), Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace.
• **Local Consignment Shops** – many music stores will hold and sell for a commission.
• **Community Boards** – university bulletin boards, local music forums, or neighborhood apps like Nextdoor. | Multiple platforms increase exposure; consignment shops handle shipping and may fetch higher prices. | | **6. Create Your Listing** | • Title: “Acoustic Guitar – [Brand] [Model] – [Year] – Excellent Condition”
• Upload all photos.
• Set a starting price slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation.
• Specify shipping options (buyer pays, free shipping, local pickup only). | A professional listing stands out and reduces back‑and‑forth. | | **7. Handle Inquiries Promptly** | • Respond within 24 hrs.
• Offer to send additional photos or a video demo if requested.
• Be honest about any issues. | Quick replies keep potential buyers engaged and show you’re serious. | | **8. Negotiate & Finalize** | • Decide beforehand your lowest acceptable price.
• Counter offers politely; consider bundling accessories (case, strap, tuner) to sweeten the deal.
• Once agreed, confirm payment method (PayPal, Venmo, cash). | Clear communication prevents misunderstandings and protects both parties. | | **9. Secure Payment & Shipping** | • For online sales, use PayPal Goods & Services or a verified Venmo transaction.
• Ship with a reputable carrier (UPS, USPS, FedEx) and insure the package.
• Use a sturdy hard case or a padded gig bag with foam inserts. | Protects against fraud and ensures the guitar arrives safely. | | **10. Leave Feedback & Follow Up** | • After delivery, leave positive feedback if satisfied.
• Ask the buyer to do the same. | Builds your reputation for future sales. | ### Quick Tips - **Bundle Extras**: Adding a new case, strap, or a set of premium strings can justify a higher price. - **Timing**: Listings posted mid‑week often receive more views than weekend posts. - **Safety**: Meet in public places for local transactions; verify payment before handing over the instrument. Good luck with your sale! If you need help drafting a description or choosing a platform, just let me know.
